definitions.explanation: A theatrical genre or work intended to amuse, as opposed to tragedy. Also used more broadly to describe absurd or laughable real-life situations.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{映画|えいが}→映画：02273_eiga⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{喜劇|きげき}だ。
シェイクスピア⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{悲劇|ひげき}→悲劇：03577_higeki⟧⟦だけでなく→〜だけでなく：18373_dakedenaku⟧{喜劇|きげき}⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{書|か}いた→書く：00477_kaku⟧。
examples.english: Shakespeare wrote comedies as well as tragedies.

examples.japanese: あまり⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦{失敗|しっぱい}→失敗：01636_shippai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{続|つづ}いて→続く：00903_tsuzuku⟧、もはや{喜劇|きげき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ような⟦{状況|じょうきょう}→状況：01576_joukyou⟧になってしまった。
examples.english: So many failures piled up that the situation became almost like a comedy.

notes:
{喜劇|きげき} refers to comedy as a theatrical or literary genre, and can also describe absurd real-life situations.

FORMS:
{喜|き} (joy) + ⟦{劇|げき}→劇：02713_geki⟧ (drama, play).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {喜劇|きげき}⟦{映画|えいが}→映画：02273_eiga⟧: comedy film
- {喜劇|きげき}⟦{俳優|はいゆう}→俳優：03547_haiyuu⟧: comedy actor, comedian
- {喜劇|きげき}⟦{作家|さっか}→作家：01414_sakka⟧: comedy writer
- {喜劇|きげき}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧ような⟦{状況|じょうきょう}→状況：01576_joukyou⟧: a situation like a comedy (absurd)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{悲劇|ひげき}→悲劇：03577_higeki⟧: tragedy (the direct opposite pair)
- ⟦コメディ→コメディ：10854_komedi⟧: comedy (loanword, more common for modern entertainment — TV, film)
- {喜劇|きげき} has a more classical or literary nuance, fitting for theatrical and academic contexts

USAGE:
Can describe absurd real-life situations: もはや{喜劇|きげき}だ (it's practically a comedy at this point).
